context: A uni student debates a teacher on civic responsibility
purpose: Teach: 社会党/歳出/不定期/追跡/延期/負傷/言動/無責任

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先生、旧社会党の路線って、結局は無責任な理想論じゃなかったですか。
lines.en: Professor, wasn't the old Socialist Party's platform basically an irresponsible idealism?
lines.style: challenging tone, leans forward slightly, blunt academic provocation

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: そう決めつけるのは早いわ。歳出削減を提唱しながら福祉を守ろうとした議員もいたのよ。
lines.en: Don't jump to conclusions. Some lawmakers advocated spending cuts while still protecting welfare.
lines.style: measured, corrective, the patient voice of a seasoned lecturer

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: でも有権者の言動を追跡してみると、結局みんな自分の利益しか見てないですよ。
lines.en: But if you track voter behavior, everyone just looks out for their own interests.
lines.style: cynical, slightly worked up, gesturing with one hand

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: だからこそ市民教育が必要なの。投票を不定期な気分で済ませてはいけないわ。
lines.en: That's exactly why civic education matters. Voting shouldn't be a casual, occasional whim.
lines.style: firm, principled, gently scolding but warm underneath

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 選挙のたびに公約が延期されて、デモで負傷者まで出る始末ですよ。
lines.en: Promises get postponed every election, and protests even end with people getting injured.
lines.style: frustrated, voice rising, listing grievances rapidly

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: それを嘆くだけで何もしないなら、あなたこそ無責任なのではない?
lines.en: If you only lament it and do nothing, aren't you the irresponsible one?
lines.style: sharp counterstrike, raised eyebrow, calm but cutting

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ……痛いところを突きますね。じゃあ僕は何から始めればいいんですか。
lines.en: ...That hits a nerve. So where am I supposed to start, then?
lines.style: deflated, conceding, scratching the back of his neck

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: まずは地元の議会を傍聴することね。怒るより、知ることのほうがずっと力になるわ。
lines.en: Start by sitting in on the local assembly. Knowing is far more powerful than anger.
lines.style: encouraging, mentor-like, softening into a genuine smile
